fieldDescription: Steers your fleet while it's flying itself to a planet, star, jump point, gate or star system. It won't steer for stations, fleets or other objects. Holding a mouse button, the go-slow key, Sensor Burst or Interdiction Pulse gives you control back for that moment.
Slows down inside and just ahead of storming or signaling cells, then burns back up after. The game doesn't strike fleets that are moving slowly.
Goes around a storm on the way to the target if the detour is short enough. Otherwise it just slows down and goes through.

fieldName: Storm detour limit (percent of the leg)
fieldDescription: The longest detour around a storm it'll take, as a percent of the distance to the target.
After leaving a slipstream, it fights the sideways speed first and then turns back to the target right away.
Hops on a nearby slipstream when it flows toward the target and saves time, and gets off where the trip ends up shortest.
The biggest angle between the stream's flow and the direction to the target where it'll still get on.
It only gets on a slipstream when the trip takes at least this percent less time.
If you have the ability, it turns Reverse Polarity on before entering or crossing a slipstream that flows away from the target, and off after leaving. Outside a slipstream that's free.
Also turns Reverse Polarity on inside a slipstream that's carrying you away from the target. That costs fuel and CR like doing it by hand, so it's skipped when a ship's CR is below the cost.

Without a usable Reverse Polarity, it stays out of a slipstream on the way that doesn't flow toward the target. If the target's on this side it goes along the edge. If it's across, it crosses straight over at a gap or the weakest spot near the way, with Sustained Burn off.

Steers around star coronas, black hole event horizons and stars (pulsar beams aren't steered around). If your course is to a star, a black hole or a point inside a corona, it stops outside and ends the course there.
Extra distance it keeps from hazards and stars, on top of the fleet's radius.

fieldName: Slow down in asteroid belts and fields
fieldDescription: Slows down inside asteroid belts and fields, starting at braking distance before them, then burns back up after. Slow-moving fleets don't take asteroid impacts.

fieldName: Burn out of coronas and pulsar beams
fieldDescription: If a corona, a black hole or a pulsar beam holds the fleet back so it can't get closer to the target for 4 seconds, it turns Sustained Burn off for full acceleration. If that's not enough, it uses Emergency Burn, but only when every ship has the CR for it, so nothing takes damage. Close to the target, Sustained Burn goes off right away.

fieldName: Transverse Jump out of pulsar beams
fieldDescription: If a pulsar beam still holds the fleet after normal burn and Emergency Burn (or those can't be used), it uses Transverse Jump to get out into hyperspace. That costs fuel and CR like doing it by hand. If your target is in that same system, the course gets cleared once you're out, so it doesn't fly you straight back into the beam.
Steers around hostile fleets you can see, that can see you and that are stronger than you. It'll fly straight past weaker ones.
A hostile fleet counts as stronger when its effective strength is above yours times this number.
How far it stays from stronger hostile fleets, added to both fleets' radii.

Turns Sustained Burn on for trips longer than 2000 units and 11 seconds, and back on if the game or another ability turned it off. Also while riding a slipstream with the flow (it goes off when you leave the stream). Not while slowing down, near a slipstream or with a stronger hostile fleet close by. If you turn it off yourself, it stays off until your next target.

Jumps into and out of star systems without the jump dialog. You'll still get the dialog when the game would warn you about hostile fleets at the exit, ask about your transponder, or you're short on fuel, and for wormholes, unstable jump points and jump points with more than one exit. Fuel is the same as a normal jump.

A laid-in course goes through two gates of one network when that's at least the percent below and one light year shorter. This needs Travel through the Gate (Janus Device working, At the Gates finished), and it uses scanned active gates, plus gate beacons as exits only (like a Random Assortment of Things settlement with a Gate Beacon). It flies to the entry gate, goes through without the gate dialog at the game's fuel cost, and lays your course back in on the other side. With hostile fleets near the exit gate or not enough fuel, it skips the transit and lays your course back in. Laying in the same course again during a gate route flies direct. It's off while the Autopilot With Gates ability is on.

With AoTD Vaults of Knowledge and a Bifrost Control Center on a colony, gate routes also use Bifrost gates that are supplied and not cooling down. A Bifrost transit costs no fuel and puts both gates on a 30-day cooldown, unless a hypershunt powers them.
Gate routes won't use a gate in a system with a pulsar (game gates, gate beacons and Bifrost gates), since coming out there can drop you right in the beam.
It only uses gates when the way through them is at least this percent and one light year shorter.
Writes each steering change, why it isn't steering, the obstacles it found for each target and a status line every 10 seconds to starsector.log. Nothing shows up on screen.
